To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Li-ion battery ageing is a complex phenomenon which is influenced by several factors.
the Li-ion ageing estimation is a complex task and it requires the development of a model that can accurately estimate battery ageing in terms of SoH and EoL.

the Li-ion battery ageing is an important factor in EVs and HEVs, and that the Li-ion batteries are the most promising candidates for EVs and HEV applications, but the battery ageing and health monitoring are the major issues for Li-ion battery applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: a) review of the current research on Li-ion ageing estimation, b) analysis of the various techniques and algorithms used for ageing estimation and health assessment, c) comparison of the techniques and algorithms based on the performance parameters such as accuracy, computational time, etc., d) identification of the gaps in the current techniques and algorithms, e) identification of the challenges in the development of a reliable and accurate ageing estimation technique, and f) future research direction.
the development of a new model for the estimation of Li-ion battery capacity fade, which is based on the analysis of the battery ageing mechanism and the experimental data of the ageing test.
battery ageing estimation, health and EoL estimation techniques.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many researches in the field of ageing estimation but still there is no standard technique for battery ageing and health estimation and there is still a need for further research.

the most accurate and reliable technique to estimate battery ageing is to use the battery itself as a source of information and to develop models and algorithms based on its electrochemical properties.
there is no single model or method which can be used as a universal approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most accurate estimation is possible through the combined use of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and capacity fade measurements, which is also the most expensive and time consuming.
the current state of research in the field of battery ageing estimation is promising.
the most promising techniques are based on machine learning algorithms, which are more accurate and reliable in terms of battery ageing prediction and health monitoring.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the battery ageing estimation is an interdisciplinary field which requires the expertise of battery engineers, electrical engineers and mathematicians.
the existing techniques and models are not sufficient to monitor the ageing of Li-ion batteries.
there is a need for more research on battery ageing and health monitoring.
